subject: Sending Data From Client to Server onload

messages.author: cd61dc1508286cb5
messages.subject: Sending Data From Client to Server onload
parts:
Hi,

I've just read http://www.r-bloggers.com/sending-data-from-client-to-server-and-back-using-shiny/

and want to do the same but when the page is loaded at the first time. Here's my code in ui.R:

 tags$script('
          window.onload = function() {
            var number = Math.random();
            Shiny.onInputChange("mydata", number);
          };
          ')

However, this code works only on Mozilla. IE and Chrome don't send "mydata" to server.R.

Is there any method how to accomplish this task?

I'm using IE 11, Firefox 35, and Chrome 41.

Thanks

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Sending Data From Client to Server onload
parts:
Shiny does its work at onload time too. It's ugly, but perhaps use a setInterval to try repeatedly until Shiny.onInputChange is present. Either that, or call session$sendCustomMessage from the server when the session begins and have the custom message handler do the work you're trying to do in onload.

Ideally we would have an event for this, it's something we've considered but not acted on. Can you tell us what your use case is for executing JS at startup?

messages.subject: Re: Sending Data From Client to Server onload
parts:
Hi Joe,

Sorry for late reply. it's GMT+7 here :).
I'm thinking about integrating authentication using PHP and shiny. At the 1st time, users are required to input user and password (1st page).
After authentication success, PHP will redirect the users to another page (2nd page) with full iframe. That's where shiny is loaded.

In the 2nd page, there are 2 javascript variables defined as below:
<script type="text/javascript">
document.domain = "SERVER_HOSTNAME";
var p_un= "<?php echo $encrypted_username; ?>";
var p_token = "<?php echo $encrypted_password; ?>";
</script>
<iframe src="http://SERVER_HOSTNAME:666" frameborder="0"></iframe>

I know this leads to vulnerability, that's why I encrypt the variables. un and token will be validated in database later.
in the ui.R file, they will be sent to server at startup:
  tags$script('
          window.onload = setTimeout(function() {
            document.domain = "SERVER_HOSTNAME";
            var s_un = parent.p_un;
            var s_token = parent.p_token;
            Shiny.onInputChange("un", s_un);
            Shiny.onInputChange("token", s_token);
          },1000);
          ')

using setTimeout, the variables are read successfully in Chrome and Mozilla, but not for IE. See error below:

This is interesting since Not implemented only happens if I'm using iframe. If I execute shiny page directly, the code runs smoothly on all browsers. (of course I need to change s_un and s_token value to something else. E.g.: s_un = Math.random())

Any ideas ? :)

Thanks

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Sending Data From Client to Server onload
parts: Encrypted or no, do not make your auth credentials accessible via JavaScript, especially in an environment like Shiny where it is so common to run third party Javascript code. The best solution is to use Shiny Server Pro where we have thought through all of these problems and solved them. If you really cannot use our commercial software then focus on an approach that protects the R process from ever even seeing unauthenticated traffic. Trying to auth after the browser has already connected to Shiny is too late.
